verses.text: Now the LORD had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house, unto a land that I will shew thee:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now the LORD had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house, unto a land that I will shew thee:

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: That is all Abram got at the start, Church. Leave your country, your kin and your father's house, and go to a land I will show you. No map. No address. Just a word from God and a promise.

verses.text: And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing:

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: God promised to make him a great nation, to bless him, and that through him all the families of the earth would be blessed. There was one problem. Abram and his wife Sarai had no children, and they were not young.

verses.text: So Abram departed, as the LORD had spoken unto him; and Lot went with him: and Abram was seventy and five years old when he departed out of Haran.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Abram departed, as the LORD had spoken unto him; and Lot went with him: and Abram was seventy and five years old when he departed out of Haran.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Seventy-five years old. Abram packed up his household, his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, everything they had and the people who worked for them, and set out for Canaan. Most folks that age are settling in. Abram started over.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Years went by. Abram moved through the land God promised. He built altars and called on the name of the LORD. But still, no child.

verses.text: After these things the word of the LORD came unto Abram in a vision, saying, Fear not, Abram: I am thy shield, and thy exceeding great reward.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After these things the word of the LORD came unto Abram in a vision, saying, Fear not, Abram: I am thy shield, and thy exceeding great reward.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Fear not, Abram. God came to him in a vision and told him he was his shield and his great reward. But Abram was honest about what was on his heart.

verses.text: And Abram said, Lord GOD, what wilt thou give me, seeing I go childless, and the steward of my house is this Eliezer of Damascus?

segments.speaker: abram
segments.text: Lord GOD, what wilt thou give me, seeing I go childless, and the steward of my house is this Eliezer of Damascus?

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: He reminded God he still had no child. As things stood, a servant from Damascus would inherit it all. He was asking the question he had carried for years. Lord, what about the promise?

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: God told him that servant would not be his heir. A son of his own would be.

verses.text: And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Imagine that night. An old man stepping out of his tent. A desert sky with no city lights and more stars than anybody could count. And God telling him, so shall thy seed be.

verses.text: And he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Say it with me. Somebody say, he believed. [PAUSE 3s | screen: "He believed"] He believed. [PAUSE 3s | screen: "He believed"] No baby yet, just a sky full of stars and a word from God.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: He believed in the LORD. Abram did not have that child yet. He had a sky full of stars and a word from God. And he believed, and God counted it to him for righteousness.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Abram's story is not a story of quick answers. More years would pass before the promised son was born. But that night, he looked up, he listened, and he trusted the God who called him out of his father's house.
